subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Lesson 6: Writing – an email (a personal profile)
outcomes: Use quite and very correctly with adjectives.
Join ideas with and, but, or, because and so.
Plan and write a clear email of about 100 words.

tf.why: Yes: very = stronger, quite = less strong.
'Quite' goes before the article: 'quite an interesting story'.
'Very' goes after the article: 'a very good film'.

tf.s: We can say 'I was very terrified'.
tf.why: 'Terrified' is an extreme adjective, so we don't use very or quite.
Yes, 'but' shows a different or opposite idea.
'So' gives a result; 'because' gives a reason.

tf.s: Each content point in your email should have some extra information.
tf.why: Details, reasons or examples make your email better.
Yes, each paragraph matches one of her notes.
Yes: 'I'm fed up with the rain.'

boxes.q: Which linking word gives a reason?
Which linking word gives a result?
boxes.why: 'So' shows what happens as a result.

boxes.q: Which linking word gives an alternative?

boxes.why: 'Quite' comes before 'an': quite an exciting day.

boxes.q: What should the last paragraph of your Channel 1 email do?
o: Say why they should choose you
boxes.why: Finish by giving reasons to choose you.

boxes.q: 'I do karate once a week' is about…
How long should your email be?
boxes.why: The task asks for about 100 words.

hunt.q: I hate speaking in public. I'm not very…

mcq.q: What does 'quite' do to an adjective?
What are the four content points in the Channel 1 email?
o: Where you live, your personality, what you enjoy, why they should choose you
Your age, your phone, your food, your bus
Your teacher, your marks, your bag, your desk
The weather, the news, sport, music
mcq.why: These four points tell Channel 1 about you.
'Very' goes after 'a': a very old village.

mcq.q: What is a school council member?
o: A parent who drives the bus
mcq.why: Council members speak for their classmates.

mcq.q: Join with the best word: I was tired. I went to bed early.
mcq.why: Going to bed early is the result, so we use 'so'.

mcq.q: Rewrite: I don't like speaking in public. → I'm not a very ___ person.
mcq.why: Not confident means you don't like speaking in public.

mcq.q: Choose the correct sentence for your email.
o: Choose me because I'm a very funny person.
Choose me because I'm very a funny person.
Choose me so I'm a funny very person.
Choose me because I'm quite a funny a person.
mcq.why: 'Because' gives the reason, and 'a very funny' is the right order.

mcq.q: Why is 'I was very terrified' wrong?
mcq.why: We don't use very or quite with extreme adjectives.

o: She covers all the points and adds extra information.
It only talks about the weather.
mcq.why: Covering every point with details makes an email strong.

mcq.q: Your partner's email misses one content point. What is the best feedback?
o: Maybe next time you could add that point.
mcq.why: Kind and useful feedback helps your partner improve.
